Subject: Clarifying how prefix reuse and minimum billing will show up on invoice

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team is working through the draft SOW and a couple of open billing points came up that we need clarified before legal signs off. Can you confirm the following so I can pass to my finance lead?

1) If we send requests that reuse a common prefix (e.g., user history or product catalog injected as a prompt), how does that prefix reuse factor into token accounting across sessions? Is there any prefix deduping or KV-cache reuse that reduces billable tokens?

2) We have frequent microcalls under 120 tokens — how does the min-floor/rounding apply (per-call minimum vs session amortization)? Provide an invoice-friendly example so we can map it to our bookkeeping.

3) If we exceed a context-length threshold (e.g., switching to 32k model), will the invoice show separate line items per model/context bucket or a blended unit? We need line-item clarity for internal chargebacks.

Appreciate short, example-driven answers. Sarah

--

Subject: Re: Clarifying how prefix reuse and minimum billing will show up on invoice

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — good questions. I put together a short explanation and asked Ben to include concrete math and an example invoice CSV (attached) so your finance team can reconcile quickly. High level:

- Prefix reuse: we do not dedupe arbitrary prompt text across independent API calls by default. However, when requests hit the same model instance and the runtime can reuse the KV cache (same conversation id / pinned session), token reuse reduces compute and therefore billable tokens in practice. For hosted customers, we expose two behaviors:
  * Session-affinity (recommended for high prefix reuse): persistent KV cache across calls — reduces billable input tokens for repeated prefixes.
  * Stateless calls (default for webhooks): each call is charged on full tokenized input.

- Minimums & rounding: we apply a per-call floor only for the smallest plan types. For enterprise customers on committed capacity (like BrightCart), we amortize microcalls across the billing window and apply a monthly minimuming policy (microfloor amortization). That means you will see fewer spiky per-call minimum line items and instead a smoothing credit in the invoice.

- Context/model transitions: invoices list model-level line items. If you use both 8k and 32k models in the billing window, you will see separate line rows for each SKU (model+quantization profile). We do not blend autonomous rates on the invoice by default — blending is done in contract language if you prefer a single blended rate.

Ben will drop the sample calculations; Kim, can you weigh in on legal-friendly invoice phrasing in the SOW?

Naomi

Sarah — attaching example-invoice.csv and a short note (tokenization-examples.pdf) with calculations. Key points and one worked example below.

Short answers first:
- No automatic global prompt dedupe; reuse only counts when KV cache/session-affinity reduces input tokens server-side.
- For enterprise commit customers we amortize microcall flooring across the month (smoothing) and issue a single smoothing credit line rather than many per-call floors.
- Model/context changes produce separate invoice lines (SKU per model).

Worked example (numbers illustrative):
- BrightCart calls: 1,200,000 calls in month, of which 800,000 are stateless microcalls (avg 90 tokens input + 10 tokens output), and 400,000 are session-affinitive with a 300-token shared prefix and 40-token variable portion.

A. Stateless microcalls billing (per-call charging):
- Tokenization rounds to nearest token; we count 90+10 = 100 tokens per call = 100 tokens * 800,000 = 80,000,000 tokens billed.
- Per-call minimum (only for small-uncommitted accounts) is not applied here because you're on a committed enterprise plan and microcall amortization applies. Instead, amortized floor credit reduces net billed tokens by roughly 0.5% in this example (see invoice credit line).

B. Session-affinitive calls with prefix reuse:
- Each session keeps a KV cache containing the 300-token prefix. Subsequent calls referencing that cache only bill the 40-token variable portion (plus any single time charge to populate the cache).
- First call per session: 300+40 = 340 tokens billed. Next 9 calls: 40 tokens billed each. So ten calls total bill = 340 + (9*40) = 700 tokens for 10 calls = 70 tokens/call on average (vs 340 if stateless).

C. Model switch / invoice mapping:
- 8k model usage: 60,000,000 tokens -> line item "redwood.gen.8k - tokens: 60,000,000"
- 32k model usage: 20,000,000 tokens -> line item "redwood.gen.32k - tokens: 20,000,000"
- Smoothing credit: line item "microfloor smoothing credit: -400,000 tokens" (applied before $ calculation)

Bottom-line invoice effect (simplified):
- Net tokens billed after smoothing: 79,600,000 tokens across SKUs (separate rows).
- Dollars calculated per SKU based on contracted per-token rates; credits applied as separate negative line items so accounting can map.

Attachments: example-invoice.csv has a sample breakdown with columns: date, sku, tokens_raw, smoothing_credit_tokens, net_tokens, unit_price, line_amount. tokenization-examples.pdf shows the token math and the session-affinity lifecycle.

If you'd like, we can:
- Add a line in the SOW that specifies "invoice line items will be broken out per model SKU and smoothing credits will be applied as separate negative rows", or
- Offer a blended invoice (single line) for accounting ease at a small additive admin fee.

Next step? If ProcureOps wants the SOW language, Kim can draft the clause.

Ben
